introduce.heroSubtitle: Research for a sustainable built energy environment

carbonNeutral.heroDesc: District building energy modeling (DBEM) for load-sharing communities predicts and evaluates building- and household-level loads, achieving community-level energy and carbon reduction through optimal load-flattening control.
carbonNeutral.overview: As rapid urbanization intensifies energy supply and demand challenges, strategies for reducing energy and carbon at the community scale, rather than the individual building scale, are increasingly needed. This project develops a district building energy modeling method for load-sharing communities, predicting and evaluating building- and household-level loads and deriving community-wide load patterns that account for interactions between buildings. It further applies optimal control technology that links the predictions to a shared management system to flatten and adjust loads, achieving community-level energy and carbon reduction.
carbonNeutral.researchContent: A hybrid district building energy model (DBEM) captures spatial interactions arising from building geometry and, based on predicted occupant behavior, evaluates heterogeneous load schedules by building use and household along with uncertainty across spatial and temporal resolutions. An integrated control strategy links a central heat pump water heater (CHPWH) based load-sharing system with renewable generation such as photovoltaics, and these component technologies are combined into a community-level optimal design and operation algorithm covering building layout, system selection, load shifting, offsetting, and generation interactions.
carbonNeutral.summary: Derives community-wide load patterns using district building energy modeling (DBEM) for load-sharing communities and applies optimal load-flattening control

dataNet.heroDesc: A national-scale data framework that links and integrates 17 administrative datasets by address, centered on the building register and energy consumption databases, to analyze the factors driving building energy consumption. BEE Lab develops building shape, form, and shading indicators to conduct energy performance diagnosis and benchmarking research.
dataNet.overview: DataNet is a project to build a national-scale data framework that links and integrates 17 administrative datasets by address, centered on the building register and energy consumption databases, enabling analysis of the various factors that influence building energy consumption.
dataNet.researchContent: The Building Environment and Energy (BEE) Lab develops building shape, form, and shading indicators. It analyzes the relationships and effects between each indicator and total energy use and heating and cooling levels, and uses these findings to conduct shape-based energy performance diagnosis and benchmarking research.
dataNet.subtitle: A Data Framework Based on the Integrated National Building Energy Database
dataNet.summary: A national-scale data framework that links and integrates 17 administrative datasets by address and diagnoses and benchmarks energy performance using building form and shading indicators

greenRemodeling.heroDesc: Quantitatively verifies the effectiveness of Green Remodeling projects that improve the energy performance of aging buildings through post-occupancy performance evaluation, and identifies the causes of gaps between design-stage predictions and actual as-built performance.
greenRemodeling.overview: Green Remodeling is a national policy program that systematically improves the energy performance of aging public and private buildings. BEE Lab conducts post-occupancy performance evaluations of buildings that have completed Green Remodeling to quantitatively verify the program's effectiveness and identify the causes of gaps between design-stage predictions and actual as-built performance.
greenRemodeling.researchContent: Material and equipment test reports are reviewed, and energy performance is calculated through ECO2-OD simulation. On-site measurements verify window shading performance through SHGC measurement, and thermal imaging cameras diagnose thermal bridges at exterior wall corners and around windows to assess construction quality.
greenRemodeling.summary: A program that quantitatively verifies the gap between design predictions and actual as-built performance through post-occupancy evaluation of buildings that have completed Green Remodeling
greenRemodeling.title: Green Remodeling Regional Hub Platform

lhGeothermal.overview: A research service commissioned by the Korea Land and Housing Corporation (LH) and conducted by the Korea Society of Geothermal and Hydrothermal Energy, targeting geothermal heat pump systems installed in apartment complexes. It aims to diagnose the gap between design performance and actual operating performance using field measurement data, and to establish a sustainable management system that addresses early-occupancy complaints and the limitations of long-term operation.
lhGeothermal.researchContent: During commissioning and the early occupancy period, temperature, flow rate, and power data are collected to analyze hourly COP and efficiency, and operational problems such as flow imbalances and control errors are diagnosed and improved. The project also reviews the feasibility (economic viability) of introducing auxiliary heat sources, establishes maintenance standards and manuals for each piece of equipment, develops a household-level billing scheme, and standardizes monitoring, including sensor specifications and guidelines.
lhGeothermal.summary: Verifies performance based on field measurement data from geothermal heat pump systems in apartment complexes, and derives measures for operational improvement, maintenance, and monitoring standardization.
lhGeothermal.title: Field Measurement-Based Performance Monitoring of Geothermal Systems in Apartment Complexes

llm.abstract: Reviews recent research trends in LLM-based multi-agent systems for building energy optimization. Analyzes the potential and limitations of LLM applications in areas such as building energy simulation, equipment control, and diagnostics.

roomvent.abstract: A paper presented at the ROOMVENT 2026 international conference, evaluating the energy performance of a data center cooling system using a water-source heat pump. Published by EDP Sciences, 14 pages, in parallel English and Korean text.
roomvent.title: Energy Performance Evaluation of a WWHP-Based Data Center Cooling System

whr.abstract: This study proposes a data center waste heat recovery system based on a water-source heat pump (WWHP) using thermal energy from the Han River. The system's energy performance was evaluated through annual dynamic simulation using TRNSYS, and the energy savings compared to a conventional air-cooled cooling system were quantitatively analyzed.

beSystems.heroOverview: The Building Energy Systems group analyzes and optimizes the energy performance of building-level equipment systems, aiming to realize efficient and sustainable buildings. It researches practical energy-saving measures through dynamic simulation using tools such as TRNSYS and EnergyPlus.
beSystems.heroSub: Design, simulation, and optimization of mechanical and equipment systems within buildings

dataAnalysis.heroOverview: The Building Data Analytics & AI group analyzes diverse data in the building energy domain to understand energy consumption structures and identify ways to improve efficiency. Using statistical models and machine learning, it researches energy diagnosis and benchmarking, urban energy demand forecasting and optimization, and occupancy and indoor environment analysis.
dataAnalysis.heroSub: Collection, analysis, and AI-based forecasting and optimization of building energy data

urbanModeling.heroOverview: The Urban Building Energy Modeling (UBEM) group models building energy environments capable of analyzing energy use from the individual building to the urban scale, in support of carbon neutrality in the building sector. Using EnergyPlus as the simulation engine, it develops building energy simulation (BEM) and urban building energy simulation (UBEM) to derive energy-saving measures and support policy decision-making.
urbanModeling.heroSub: Energy modeling, digital twins, and GIS-based analysis at the building and urban scales

journalIndex.title: Journal Metrics Comparison Table

pickATime.summary: Gathers everyone's available times on a single screen to schedule a meeting. Times marked by dragging overlap as a heatmap, and you can also open slots in advance to accept bookings. Confirmed times can be exported to your calendar.
pickATime.title: Meeting Time Coordination

ubeePlatform.summary: Quickly predicts solar radiation conditions and energy use based on urban building information and surrounding environmental data. Provides key influencing factor analysis, LLM-based result interpretation, and automatic generation of energy analysis reports.
ubeePlatform.title: UBEE Platform
